issues.body: The response body is decoded before the parse-error handler, but UnicodeDecodeError is not caught. A malformed or intercepted response containing invalid UTF-8 therefore produces a traceback and exit code 1, while the documented contract says network/parse failures return 2 so wrappers cannot confuse failure states. The official sparse index should provide UTF-8 JSON, making this a robustness issue rather than a blocker.
issues.fix_hint: Decode inside the parsing try block and include UnicodeDecodeError in the caught exceptions, or add it to the preceding request/read exception handler, then add a focused self-test for the exit-code contract if practical.
issues.title: Non-UTF-8 index responses bypass the documented indeterminate exit path

verdict.summary: The release watcher is correctly scoped as a non-gating developer tool, distinguishes network/parse indeterminacy from a negative release result, filters yanked and prerelease versions, compares unsorted index entries, and has a meaningful hermetic self-test wired into docs-quality CI. The accompanying documentation consistently preserves the local-patch and conformance/security constraints around eventual unvendoring. One minor robustness gap remains in handling a malformed non-UTF-8 index response, but it does not undermine the normal crates.io sparse-index path or justify blocking this change.
